title: Position launch starter kit: mentor rotations and outcomes
content:
Purpose:
This starter kit is a compact, action-oriented template for launching a new technical IC or manager role with a built-in mentor rotation and measurable outcomes. Intended for hiring managers + people ops to use when opening a req and for the hiring packet given to new hires on day zero.

Quick summary (one line):
Reduce time-to-first-meaningful-PR and first-quarter impact by pairing planned mentor rotations, focused 30/60/90 outcomes, and a lightweight hiring rubric.

Scope and when to use:
- New ICs (SWE/MLE/SRE) and first-line managers joining product or platform teams.
- Use this as the default for roles that require cross-functional ramping (product, infra, platform, SRE).
- Not for short-term contractors < 30 days.

Hiring plan sketch (timeline):
- Week -6: Kickoff with hiring manager, final role draft, target candidate profile, salary band check, interview panel identified.
- Week -5: Sourcing launch, quick recruiter screen script, start pipeline.
- Week -4 to -2: Screen loop (recruiter -> hiring manager -> technical -> behavioral), weekly syncs with recruiter.
- Week -1: Final on-site/callback, comp calibration, reference check starts.
- Day 0: Offer acceptance, welcome packet + assigned mentor rotation calendar sent.

Interview rubric (compact, shared with panel):
Scoring guide (0-3):
0 = No evidence / can't assess
1 = Partial / needs strong coaching to hit bar
2 = Solid / meets expectations for level
3 = Exceeds / clear evidence of going beyond expectations

Core dimensions (panel should score each):
- Technical problem solving (algorithms, system design where appropriate)
- Product sense / tradeoffs (for product-facing roles)
- Code fluency and ownership (readability, tests, pragmatic refactor)
- Collaboration & communication (async + sync)
- Reliability & operational thinking (for infra / SRE)
- Culture & learning orientation (curiosity, ownership)

Hiring manager guidance: prefer consistent middle ground — a candidate with multiple 2s and at least one 3 should be strongly considered. Any 0 in a critical dimension -> escalate.

Sample behavioral prompts (for panel):
- Tell us about a time you simplified a complex system under time pressure. What tradeoffs did you make?
- Describe a cross-team disagreement you led through. What was your approach to reach a solution?
- For manager candidates: how do you balance shipping vs coaching? Give a concrete example.

Offer & acceptance checklist (operations):
- Offer packet prepared: comp, equity, manager intro note, expected start date, equipment plan.
- IT access pre-reqs: HR form, payroll, corporate laptop order, VPN access request to infra team.
- Compliance: NDA signed, background check scheduled (if required).
- Day 0 asset: welcome doc with calendar for mentor rotations, Slack intro template, 30/60/90 outcomes.

Onboarding: mentor-rotation model (named and sequenced)
Idea: rotate the new hire through 3 short mentor pairings in the first 6 weeks so they see product, infra, and partner-team perspectives. Each rotation = 2 weeks of focused pairing and 1 async deliverable.
- Mentor A (week 0-2): Team codebase owner — goal: get a small bugfix or doc PR merged. Deliverable: merged PR + 1-page architecture note.
- Mentor B (week 2-4): Product or feature PM/owner — goal: scope a small customer-facing change and draft test plan. Deliverable: scoped mini-spec + acceptance criteria.
- Mentor C (week 4-6): Ops/SRE or partner infra — goal: run a canary deploy/test and capture runbook gap. Deliverable: runbook update + incident postmortem template filled for a hypothetical outage.
Notes: mentors should block 4 hours/week for pairing, and contribute to the final 1:1 with manager at week 6.

30/60/90 outcomes (examples to adapt to role):
30-day: environment setup, first merged PR, 2 shadowed triage sessions, stakeholder map completed.
60-day: lead a small scoped change end-to-end, own a pager rotation, contribute to team roadmap discussion.
90-day: independent feature delivery with owner-level QA, present a proposal for a measurable improvement (latency, cost, reliability), and a personal development plan.

Success metrics (what we track during ramp):
- Time to first merged PR (target: <= 14 days)
- Time to first owned CHURN (bug/regression closure) <= 45 days
- Manager weekly sync sentiment (satisfaction scale 1-5) — aim 4 by week 6
- Mentor feedback forms at week 2, 4, 6 (simple rubric: engagement, clarity, progress)

Access & permissions quick checklist (to push to infra prior to start):
- GitHub: repo access scaffolded to team level
- Ticketing: read/write to team's Jira board
- Slack: add to relevant channels and engineering org channel
- Cloud: dev project access, low-priv infra sandbox for experiments
- Vault/KMS: request token with expiring dev token; escalate for production keys later

Manager playbook (first 6 weeks):
- Week 0: 1:1 day 0 (welcome + expectations), schedule mentor rotations, set communication norms.
- Weekly: 1:1 + triage co-observe in week 1-3, weekly written status (1-2 bullets on progress + blockers).
- Week 3: mini-review with mentors + new hire to agree on 60-day plan.
- Week 6: formal 6-week check-in (documented), adjust scope for quarter.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mentors overloaded -> Mitigate: limit mentors to 1 active mentee at a time; budget 2 hours/week per mentee.
- Risk: new hire stuck on infra access -> Mitigate: include infra ticket for expedited access as part of offer flow.
- Risk: mismatch between expectations -> Mitigate: have an early 1:1 to align on top 3 priorities in week 1 and document them.

Artifacts to attach to the offer pack (templates):
- Welcome note (short), Day 0 schedule (hours blocked), Mentor rotation calendar (.ics), 30/60/90 template, Example PR checklist, Manager feedback form v1.

Notes to self / open questions (workpad):
- Do we enforce mentor training? maybe a 30-min short runbook for mentors — ask L&D about micro-credential.
- Should we mandate the PR target (<=14 days) across all levels? might vary by role seniority.
- Check with legal on contractor variant for mentor rotation and access rules.

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha: finalize welcome templates and attach to offer packet (due 2025-03-05).
- Diego: prototype mentor micro-training (due 2025-03-12).
- Mei: add infra expedited access ticket to offer flow (due 2025-03-01).
- Omar: incorporate rubric into the interview scheduling system (JIRA-HIRE-1293).

Endnotes: This doc is intentionally lightweight and modular — copy the mentor rotation block into role-specific onboarding packets and iterate from feedback forms.

-- a.p.
